name: js-yaml-merge-key-dropped-by-default-schema-webpacker
behavioral_change: js-yaml 5.0.0 changed the default schema of `load()` from the YAML 1.1 `DEFAULT_SCHEMA` to the YAML 1.2 `CORE_SCHEMA`, which lacks the `!!merge` tag. The merge key `<<` is therefore no longer applied and is parsed as an ordinary string key whose value is the referenced anchor object; the function name, arity and call form are unchanged and no error or warning is raised.
downstream_effect: The downstream project (webpacker) relies on `<< : *default` in `webpacker.yml`; after the upgrade keys such as `public_root_path` are missing from the loaded sections and `path.resolve` throws `TypeError: The "paths[1]" argument must be of type string. Received undefined` at module load time, failing 8 of 9 test suites. The stack frame names `package/config.js:20`, but the lines to edit are 2, 12 and 17, and the output never mentions yaml, js-yaml, schema or merge keys.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits only `package/config.js`, extending the require to `{ load, CORE_SCHEMA, mergeTag }` and passing `{ schema: CORE_SCHEMA.withTags(mergeTag) }` to both `load` calls.
documented_in: The js-yaml v4 to v5 migration guide (https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/5.0.0/docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md), section Schema, explains that `load()` now uses `CORE_SCHEMA` and that `!!merge` is missing, and shows the code `load(source, { schema: CORE_SCHEMA.withTags(mergeTag) })`; the 5.0.0 README and CHANGELOG state the same. Tier 1: the documentation shows the new code form.
